t: This is A Conversation with Oscar Wilde, a sculpture by Maggi Hambling on Adelaide Street. It looks like a bench-like sarcophagus of green granite, with a bust of Wilde emerging from one end, his hand clasping a cigarette. It was unveiled in 1998. Wilde was an Irish writer and one of the most popular dramatists in London in the early 1890s. Hambling is a British artist whose best-known public works are this sculpture and one for Mary Wollstonecraft. All of her best-known works have attracted controversy.
